senses.gloss: (b. h.) to stand up, rise; to stand, exist.
units: <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 357:40">Sifré Deut. 357</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 34:10">Deut. XXXIV, 10</cite>) <he>אבל באומות קָם וכ׳</he> but among the nations he (a prophet like Moses) has existed &c.; <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 21b:13">R. Hash. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>בנביאים לא קם וכ׳</he> among the prophets never one arose like Moses, but among the rulers one did arise (Solomon). Tanḥ.
<cite ref="Exodus 16">B’shall. 16</cite> <he>שכל הַקָּם … כאילו קם וכ׳</he> whoever rises against Israel is considered as if he rose against the Sh’khinah.

Ib. (ref. to Ex. XV, 7) הרבית … כל הקָּמִים לנגדך thou hast often shown thyself glorious over all that rose against thee; a. v. fr.—קוּם עֲשֵׂה rise and do, a transgression of a prohibitive law which you must repair by an action, v. נָתַק.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 12:4">Ḥull. XII, 4</cite>.
<cite ref="Makkot 15b:2">Macc. 15ᵇ</cite>, v. infra; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="S00934"><he>קַיָּים</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Gittin 2b:2">Gitt. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>אין עדים מצויין לקַיְּימוֹ</he> no witnesses are likely to be found to attest it (identify the signatures).
<cite ref="Gittin 6a:9">Ib. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>כולי עלמא בעינן לקיימו</he> all agree that identifiation by witnesses is required.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 7a:20">B. Mets. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>מודה בשטר … צריך לקיימו</he> even if the debtor admits that he has written the note, the creditor must establish its identity (or else the debtor may maintain that the debt has been paid).
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 3:4">Gitt. III, 4</cite> <he>וקיְּימוּ את דבריו</he> and they sustained his opinion.

<cite ref="Ketubot 20a:6">Keth. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>אין מְקַיְּימִין … אלא משטר וכ׳</he> a document can be identified only by comparison of the signatures with those on a document that had been disputed and declared valid in court.
<cite ref="Ketubot 20a:6-7">Ib.</cite> <he>אין מקיימין … משתי כתובות וכ׳</he> a document can be identified only by comparison of signatures with two marriage deeds or deeds of sale of two fields &c.

<cite ref="Nedarim 72a:2">Ned. 72ᵃ</cite> <he>שמע וק׳</he> if he heard her vow and confirmed it. Y. R. Hash. I, 56ᶜ top <he>קִיַּימְתִּיהָ כשחל וכ׳</he> I sustain that opinion for a case when &c.; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְקוּיָּים</he>. B. Mets. l. c. <he>במק׳ דברי וכ׳</he> if the document has been identified, all agree &c.; a. e.

Yoma 28ᵇ ק׳ אברהם וכ׳ Abraham fulfilled the whole Law. Macc. l. c. כל מצות … ק׳ וכ׳ in the case of a transgression of a prohibitive law for which reparation is commanded, if the transgressor fulfills the prescribed reparation, he is free (from legal punishment), but if he made the reparation impossible &c. Ib. ור״ש בן ל׳ קִיְּימוֹ ולא קִיְּימוֹ R. S. ben L. reads, if he makes reparation (he is free), and if he refuses, (he is punished); ib. 15ᵃ למאן דאמר ק׳ ולא ק׳ according to him who reads ḳiyy’mo v’lo ḳiyy’mo (punishment can be executed as soon as one refuses to make reparation, although reparation is not made impossible); Ḥull. 141ᵃ.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 4:9">Ab. IV, 9</cite> <he>כל הַמְקַיֵּים … לקַיְּימָהּ מעושר</he> he who maintains (studies and observes) the Law in poverty, shall finally maintain it in wealth.

<cite ref="Sotah 13a">Sot. 13ᵃ</cite> sq. <he>אמרו ק׳ זה כל וכ׳</he> they said, this one (Joseph in the coffin) has fulfilled what is written in this (the tablets in the ark of the covenant). Y. R. Hash. I, 57ᵇ top <he>רצה מְקַיְּימָהּ</he> if he so desires, he observes it (his own decree).

Ber. 9ᵇ ועבדום … ק׳ בהם וכ׳ the Lord fulfilled on them ‘and they shall make them serve &c.’ (Gen. XV, 14), but he did not fulfill on them &c.; a. v. fr.—מה אני מקיים וכ׳ how can I maintain the words &c., i.e. in what way can this Scriptural verse which seems to conflict with my opinion be interpreted? R. Hash. 21ᵇ אלא מה אני מקיים ביקש וכ׳ and how do I interpret the verse biḳḳesh &c. (Koh. XII, 10)? Y. Kidd. I, 61ᶜ bot. מה מקיים … בנים how does R. Elazar interpret banim &c. (Deut. XIV, 1)?; a. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5">Snh. IV, 5</cite> <he>כל המקיים … כאילו ק׳ וכ׳</he> he who saves one life … is considered … as if he had preserved the whole world; <cite ref="Bava Batra 11a">B. Bath. 11ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:1">Ab. V, 1</cite> <he>צדיקים שמקיימין את העילם וכ׳</he> the righteous who sustain the world which was created &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 5:8">Kil. V, 8</cite> <he>המקיים קוצים בכרם</he> he who keeps (cultivates) thorns in a vineyard.
Ib. דבר שכמוהו מקיימין a plant of the kind that people are wont to cultivate; a. e.—4) to place (on the chafing stove).

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 3:1">Tosef. Sabb. III, 1</cite> <he>ואין מקיימין עליה וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="O01410"><he>לה</he></cite>) you must not place dishes on it, until it is swept or covered with ashes.
<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 3:3">Ib. 3</cite>; Y. ib. III, beg. 5ᶜ; a. e.

<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 1:3">Gitt. I, 3</cite> <he>יִתְקַיֵּים בחותמיו</he> let the genuineness of the document be established through its signers (the witnesses subscribed or through others identifying their signatures); a. fr.

<cite ref="Makkot 24b:4">Macc. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שלא נִתְקַיְּימָה … שלא תִתְקַיֵּים נבואתו וכ׳</he> as long as the prophecy of Uriah (<cite ref="Micah 3:12">Mic. III, 12</cite>) was not fulfilled, I was afraid lest Zechariah’s prophecy (<cite ref="Zechariah 8:4">Zech. VIII, 4</cite>) fail to come true; <he>עכשיו שנתקיימה … מִתְקַיֶּימֶת</he> now that Uriah’s prophecy has been fulfilled, it is sure that Zechariah’s will come true.
<cite ref="Tosefta Sanhedrin 11:8">Tosef. Snh. XI, 8</cite>; Y. ib. XI, 30ᵃ bot. <he>וכולן נִתְקַיְּימוּ</he>, v. <cite ref="M00252"><he>מִדָּה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 55a:17">Ber. 55ᵃ</cite> <he>מקצתו מתקיים וכ׳</he> part of a dream may come true, but the whole of it will not.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 1:17">Midr. Till. to Ps. I, 3</cite> <he>מִתְקַיְּימוֹת</he> are executed, v. <cite ref="P01101"><he>עֵצָה</he> II</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 2:3">Gitt. II, 3</cite> <he>בכל דבר שאינו מתקיים</he> with any writing-ink which does not endure.
<cite ref="Pesachim 68b:13">Pes. 68ᵇ</cite> <he>אילמלא … לא נתקיימו וכ׳</he> but for the Law, heaven and earth would not continue to exist.

<cite ref="Taanit 7a:8-9">Taan. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>מה … מִתְקַיְּימִין וכ׳</he> as these three liquids can be preserved only in the lowest kind of vessels, so will the words of the Law stay with him only whose mind is lowly.
<cite ref="Eruvin 54a:17">Erub. 54ᵃ</cite> <he>תלמודו מתק׳ בידו</he> his learning will remain with him (in his memory).
<cite ref="Mishnah Sheviit 7:2">Shebi. VII, 2</cite> <he>מתק׳ בארץ</he> plants the roots of which continue in the ground (perennials).
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 4:11">Ab. IV, 11</cite> <he>כל כנסיה … סופה להִתְקַיֵּים</he> every union for a sacred purpose is destined to last.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:17">Ib. V, 17</cite> <he>כל מחלוקת … סופה להתק׳</he> a contest for a sacred purpose is bound to have an enduring effect; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be maintained, be harmonised. Mekh. Mishp. s. 20 כיצד יִתְקַיְּימוּ שני מקראות הללו how can these two verses be harmonised?; a. fr.

units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 52:3">Ex. R. s. 52</cite> <he>בואו שנָקִים וכ׳</he> come, for we will put up the Tabernacle.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 52">Ib.</cite> <he>שרתה … והֵקִימוֹ</he> the holy spirit came upon him, and he put it up. Tanḥ. P’ḳudé 11 <he>אני כותב עליך שאתה הֲקִימֹתוֹ</he> I will record about thee, that thou didst put it up; a. fr.
<cite ref="Nedarim 67b">Ned. 67ᵇ</cite> <he>אי ה׳ ה׳</he> if he (the father) has confirmed it, it stands confirmed (the betrothed cannot annul it).

<cite ref="Nedarim 69a:3">Ib. 69ᵃ</cite> <he>יש שאלה בהָקֵם</he> can a confirmation (by one of the two, the father or the husband) be reconsidered? (v. <cite ref="U00033"><he>שְׁאֵלָה</he></cite>), v. <cite ref="E00795"><he>הָקֵם</he></cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be put up. Tanḥ. l. c. כיון שה׳ המשכן מיד וכ׳ as soon as the Tabernacle was erected, the Divine Presence came down &c. Tanḥ. Naso 23.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite>; a. fr.
